Which positions matched, under `any_token`

Source: R/name_matching.R
name_given_match_position.Rd

Retained as evidence so a caller can weight a shared FIRST name above a shared MIDDLE name. A middle-name-only agreement is weak – common middle names collide across unrelated people – and must remain distinguishable so it is never silently promoted to identification.

Usage

name_given_match_position(a_first, b_first, a_middle = NULL, b_middle = NULL)

Arguments

a_first, b_first

`character`: given-name fields.

a_middle, b_middle

`character`: middle-name fields; may be `NULL`.

Value

`character`: `"both_leading"`, `"one_leading"`, `"neither_leading"`, or `NA` when no full token is shared.

See also

Other name-matching: NAME_SURNAME_PARTICLES, name_given_tokens(), name_leading_given(), name_matching_primitives, name_surname_components(), name_surname_match_type(), names_have_compatible_given(), names_have_compatible_surname()
